dossier.public_summary: The dip depth changes by >100 percent from sector to sector and even within the same pipeline, and individual transits vary from near-zero to very deep, with most of the signal from a few events. The transit is also much longer than expected and needs an implausible stellar density. Together this points to noise or a diluted/blended eclipsing binary, not a ~3.7 Rearth planet on this M dwarf.

reasons.why: Depth changes enormously between sectors and within the same pipeline, not a steady planet signal. This is sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with QLP p_constant 1.6071482612436512e-10.
Individual transit depths are inconsistent; top 3 out of 7 carry 0.908 of the SNR with deep outliers (2672ppm -5.1 sigma, -467ppm -5.1 sigma) so the signal is driven by a few bad events.
Transit is much longer than a central crossing for this star and requires much lower stellar density, consistent with a stellar or blended origin rather than a planet on target.
